result.response:
I have investigated the failing test case and generated the Living Requirement specification in Gherkin/BDD format.

The failing test [`TestPartial_Constructors.testConstructorEx7_TypeArray_intArray`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_1_group_d_arch/src/test/java/org/joda/time/TestPartial_Constructors.java#L260-L315) demonstrates that when passing an array of `DateTimeFieldType` where `era()` is placed after smaller units (e.g., `[year, era, monthOfYear]` or `[year, dayOfMonth, era]`), [`Partial`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_1_group_d_arch/src/main/java/org/joda/time/Partial.java#L189-L247) incorrectly accepts the array instead of throwing an `IllegalArgumentException` enforcing largest-to-smallest field ordering.

The intended behavior has been specified in [requirement.feature](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_1_group_d_arch/requirement.feature):

```gherkin
Feature: Partial constructor field order validation

  Scenario: Constructing a Partial with year before era throws IllegalArgumentException
    Given an array of field types containing "year", "era", and "monthOfYear"
    And an array of integer values [1, 1, 1]
    When a Partial is constructed with these types and values
    Then an IllegalArgumentException should be thrown indicating the types must be in order largest-smallest

  Scenario: Constructing a Partial with dayOfMonth before era throws IllegalArgumentException
    Given an array of field types containing "year", "dayOfMonth", and "era"
    And an array of integer values [1, 1, 1]
    When a Partial is constructed with these types and values
    Then an IllegalArgumentException should be thrown indicating the types must be in order largest-smallest
```
